source.paraphrase: A boolean argument that selects behavior is a flag. Replace it with two operations whose names say which behavior they run.

invariants.why: A boolean flag hides two operations behind one name. The call site reads notify(user, true) and the reader has to open the function to know what true means.
invariants.fixHint: Split into two named operations, or pass a union such as "email" | "none".
invariants.avoid: Making the flag optional, or giving it a default, keeps the flag. A boolean property on a type is not a parameter and is not this rule.

source.paraphrase: A long chain of getters means the caller knows the layout of objects it does not own. Ask the first object for the result instead.

invariants.why: The caller is navigating someone else's structure. When that structure changes, every chain breaks, which is the feature-envy smell in a form the tree can see.
invariants.fixHint: Add a method on the owner that returns the value the caller actually needs, and call that once.
invariants.avoid: Optional chaining does not shorten the chain. a.b.c is two hops and is allowed; a.b.c.d is the chain this rule rejects.

source.paraphrase: Do not leave a function that has a name and no behavior. Either it does the work or it is not in the code yet.

invariants.why: An empty body is a stub that looks finished. Callers compile against a function that does not do the thing its name says.
invariants.fixHint: Write the operation, or delete the function until there is a real body. An empty constructor can stay.
invariants.avoid: A comment inside the braces is not an implementation. Filling the body with a log line only to silence the rule is a stub of a different shape and is called out in the avoid text of the vibe-proof console rule.

source.work: Refactoring (M. Fowler) and Google TypeScript style
source.paraphrase: One conditional expression is enough. A second one inside it hides the decision.

invariants.why: A nested ternary packs two decisions into one expression. The reader cannot see which branch matches which condition without counting question marks.
invariants.fixHint: Use if statements, or a function whose name is the decision.
invariants.avoid: Parentheses around the inner ternary do not flatten it.

relations.why: Both count public methods: in use-case files CA-UC-001 allows 1 and SR-WIDE-001 allows 8, so a wide use case is reported by both.
relations.settle: Usually keep both, since CA-UC-001 is the narrower use-case rule; to report once, exclude the use-case globs from SR-WIDE-001.

source.work: A Philosophy of Software Design (J. Ousterhout, 2018)
source.paraphrase: A module should hide a lot of complexity behind a small interface. A class with a long list of public operations is a shallow module.

invariants.why: A wide class is a module that makes every caller learn a large surface. Ousterhout's deep module hides complexity behind a small interface; past eight public operations the type is doing several jobs.
invariants.fixHint: Split the class by the reason its methods change. Keep the public operations the caller actually needs.
invariants.avoid: Renaming methods to a private prefix with the private keyword or a # name removes them from the count without splitting the job. That is a hole. Arrow fields are public surface and count. The constructor does not.
